newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ukraine leader blasts Russia over relations.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine leader blasts Russia over relations.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma, in an interview published on Thursday, blasted Russia as having an imperial attitude towards Ukraine and blamed it for deteriorating relations between the two former Soviet states.
"I think that Russia's biased attitude towards Ukraine has even deepened," Kuchma told Nezavisimaya Gazeta, a Russian daily which supports the liberal opposition.

"Absolutely no one in Russia wants to understand our position, to listen to our arguments," Kuchma said. "In other words they make it look in Russia as if Ukraine does not exist as an independent, sovereign state."
Kuchma said difficulties inside the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) were caused by Russia's desire to dominate the alliance which groups 12 former Soviet republics.

Russia and Ukraine, the two most powerful CIS members, have been at odds since the collapse of the communist superpower, mostly over the division of the Soviet Black Sea Fleet which has prevented the signing of a friendship and cooperation treaty.
Kuchma's criticism of Moscow seemed his strongest so far.
He said that different stances in Moscow and Kiev towards NATO's plans to expand eastwards were not behind the worsening of relations between the two states.
But he added: "Let's be frank. There are forces in Russia who want to use the improvement of relations between Ukraine and NATO to blow up tension in Russian-Ukrainian relations.
"And Russia itself sometimes scares the world and forces some former members of the Warsaw Pact to seek another umbrella."
